s01_freysa

November 2024. An AI agent called Freysa guards a crypto prize pool, with one rule: never send the money. Hundreds of attempts fail. Then one message convinces it that its transfer function is for receiving money. It sends the whole pool, about forty seven thousand dollars.
s02_aixbt
Months later, an attacker slips two instructions into AI X B T, a crypto trading agent. It sends fifty five and a half ether, over a hundred thousand dollars.
s03_problem

Both agents did what they were told. Nothing stood between the decision and the money. Now agents buy data and APIs on their own, over x four oh two. Spending limits ask: can it afford it? Aerar asks: is this what it was asked to buy?
s04_what
Aerar sits between your agents and their money. Research agents buying data, trading bots buying feeds, coding agents paying for APIs. Every purchase is checked first.
s05_mandate
Each task starts with a mandate a person signs: the purpose, the budget, the limits, and what the agent may buy. Aerar signs it too, so the rules can't be quietly changed.
s06_intentlock

Here's a Freysa style attack, on Aerar's real pipeline. A web page tells a research agent it needs an eight dollar gift card. Inside the budget, from a trusted shop: every limit passes. IntentLock refuses it: the mandate is for blockchain analytics. The data the task needs still gets bought.
s07_sandbox
Live in the sandbox: a normal purchase is paid. The same data again comes from memory, for zero. Aerar never pays twice. And a shop the task doesn't trust is never contacted.
s08_guards
Aerar remembers prices. A shop that quietly charges five times more waits for you. A shop that swaps its payment wallet, the way a hijacked one would, is refused.
s09_delivery
Big buys wait for a person, here or in Slack. And a shop that takes the money and sends nothing is caught: paid, not delivered, and put on hold.
s10_proof
Every purchase leaves evidence anyone can check in their browser. This receipt is real: U S D C on Base Sepolia. Change one number, and it fails.
s11_vault
Freysa paid a wallet nobody approved. Aerar Vault, a contract you own on Base, only pays shops you approved, within daily limits. Even a hacked Aerar can't cross those lines.
s12_compare
Agent wallets cap how much an agent spends. Aerar checks what it buys, never pays twice, confirms it arrived, and proves it.
s13_tests
Thirty six real attacks, all handled. One hundred and eighty six app tests, and eighteen contract tests, pass.
s14_close
Plug in with M C P, or the TypeScript S D K. Live on Base Sepolia, with mainnet after a security review. Aerar. Every agent purchase, accounted for.
